minutes.headline: Select Board settled the annual town meeting consent calendar, appointed three volunteers, and moved a meeting to April 27.
minutes.summary: The board heard a skateboard park update, made appointments to the Cultural Council and Green Communities Task Force, and reviewed the annual appointment process. It voted on which warrant articles go on the consent calendar and heard the town manager's report on COVID, road work, bids and the 925 Mass Ave site. It then went into executive session on union bargaining.

public_comment.topic: Criticised the select board's proposed article to amend the APD bylaw, saying the board should have asked about preserving only the shell of the old primary school and sought a cost figure; endorsed a member for reelection.

votes.outcome: passed (roll call; one member, Ms. Adams, stated she would not support; chair's vote not clear)

votes.motion: Approve the consent calendar of warrant articles 1, 2, 3, 4, 7, 8, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 22, 23 and 27
Move the April 20 meeting to April 27 (by consensus, no objection)
Enter executive session on collective bargaining (municipal employees, fire and DPW unions) and adjourn afterward

budget_items.what_was_said: The town manager listed a small prior-year bill payment as non-controversial for the consent calendar.
Stabilization, OPEB, sewer, solid waste, water and PEG access enterprise articles were proposed for the consent calendar; a member questioned whether the sizable sewer ones should be included.
The chair reported signing an accounts payable, a payroll deduction and a payroll warrant.
figures_as_heard: eight hundred thirty nine thousand nine hundred twenty three dollars and eighty three cents

budget_items.what_was_said: The capital planning committee voted to recommend raising the base capital project threshold; it goes to the finance committee, then the board.
Six bids were received and a notice of award was issued to the low bidder; reimbursement deadline extension was requested from MassDOT.
MassDEP identified a possible LUST program funding source for cleanup before the town takes the tax title property.

budget_items.topic: APDC budget request and building projects
budget_items.what_was_said: The APDC asked for an expense line in the FY22 budget; the town manager said the budget process concluded but a request can go to fall special town meeting, and building envelope projects are on the FY22 capital plan.
A request to include the earmark in the end-of-year supplemental budget was sent, and an amendment will be filed for the FY22 state budget.
The skatepark group reported cash and in-kind donations booked to date.

decisions.decision: Consent calendar will remain a standing agenda item; the town manager will take it to the Finance Committee and the board may amend it next week if articles are pulled.
Town manager and board agreed to put making the Green Communities Task Force a standing committee on a future agenda.
Board agreed to clean up the annual appointment list so ad hoc and advisory bodies are treated consistently.
April 20 meeting cancelled; the board will meet April 27 before annual town meeting.
The town manager will notify the Cultural Council of the appointments.

what_happened.line: The Select Board approved a consent calendar of warrant articles for annual town meeting by roll call, with all ayes heard.
The board appointed two people to the Cultural Council, each with a term expiring June 30, 2024, both by roll call.
The board appointed Mr. Pacios to the Green Communities Task Force; one member said she would not support it, and the chair's vote was not clear.
The board agreed to put a standing Green Communities committee and a cleanup of the annual appointment list on future agendas.
The April 20 meeting was cancelled; the board will meet April 27, before annual town meeting.

why_it_matters: Articles on the consent calendar are voted together at town meeting without separate debate, so residents who want to discuss one, including the enterprise and stabilization articles, would need to ask for it to be pulled.
The appointment cleanup and standing-committee question decide how much public oversight ad hoc and advisory bodies get.
watch_next: The April 27 Select Board meeting, where the consent calendar may be amended if articles are pulled.
The Finance Committee review of the consent calendar and of the proposed rise in the base capital project threshold.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The records agree on the two Cultural Council appointments, the consent calendar, the Complete Streets bid, the $75,000 skate park total and the warrant amounts; most differences are misheard names and figures. The one to check is the Green Community Task Force appointment: both say 4-1, but ours puts the "no" on Ms. Adams while the official roll call has the chair, Mr. Alonzo, voting nay.
